newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy opposition demand change to house tax plans.
newsitem.headline: Italy opposition demand change to house tax plans.

text.p: Italy's opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance threatened a "revolution" unless the government scrapped plans in the 1997 budget to increase property taxes, the leader of the centrist CCD party said on Wednesday.
"The government must remove the house tax by tomorrow afternoon unless they want a revolution," Pierferdinando Casini told reporters after a meeting of Freedom Alliance heads.
"There are also other points that are unacceptable...this is a budget totally based on taxes," he added.
The budget, which was approved by cabinet last week and is due to be officially presented to parliament on Thursday, aims to cut 62.5 trillion lire off next year's projected deficit.
Casini said the centre-right was preparing a series of demonstrations to protest against the package, which would be launched in November.

Among measures included in the budget is a five percent increase in taxes on house and land ownership as well as a five percent increase in the valuations local authorities can base their property taxes on.

The plan has drawn fire from across the political spectrum with the largest party in the government coalition, the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), as well as the unions demanding alternative proposals.
The Freedom Alliance, headed by former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi, is due to present its own, "counter-budget" on Thursday.
